_about: Config for .github/scripts/{build,check,smoke}_release_tree.py (#2705, ported from claude-remember#851). The `release` branch is what the Anthropic plugin directory fetches; master keeps everything. See docs/releasing.md.
_deny_why: Deny-list, not allow-list: a path forgotten here ships and is caught loudly by the size/count check; a path forgotten in an allow-list would vanish from users' installs silently. Entry ending in '/' = directory prefix, otherwise an exact path.
_credential_presets_why: #2734: these five presets read a credential (an env var, or a config/cookie file) and send it to their own vendor's API -- bsky.app (bluesky), dev.to (devto), gql.hashnode.com (hashnode), slack.com (slack), googleapis.com (youtube) -- the shape the Anthropic directory's MCP_FORWARDS_CREDENTIAL_ENV hold fires on (#2732, release-preview, 2026-10-03). Each preset's own top-level manifest (presets/<name>.json) is denied alongside its directory, or _find_preset_file would still resolve a preset.json left over from a stale build. presets/watch/sources/bluesky-engagement/ and presets/watch/sources/devto-engagement/ read their own env vars directly (BLUESKY_APP_PASSWORD, DEVTO_API_KEY) and do not import anything from presets/bluesky/ or presets/devto/ -- confirmed by reading both poller.py files, each says so in its own module docstring. presets/watch/sources/slack/ is different: its poller.py dynamically loads presets/slack/_auth.py and presets/slack/_api.py by file path at import time (importlib.util.spec_from_file_location against _PRESETS_DIR / 'slack' / '_auth.py'), so denying presets/slack/ without also denying this source would ship a watch source whose import crashes on a file that no longer exists -- it is denied here for that reason, not named in #2734's own proposal text. presets/hashnode and presets/youtube have no watch-source counterpart (checked: no matching directory under presets/watch/sources/). dpt-plugins keeps shipping all of these from master; only the directory build (this file) omits them. _supertool_config.py's _DIRECTORY_BUILD_EXCLUDED_PRESETS must list the same five preset names, so a directory config that still declares one of them gets a message naming why, not a bare 'not found'.
_env_word_why: #2734, tenth pass: the directory's scanner reads the bare word `env` in any shipped string as `environment (printenv / env / export -p / set)` (release-preview @ b5e56fd; probe-n @ 3525eeb moved the citation by renaming one file's three; claude-directory-publishing/triggers.md, 2026-10-04). The watch op family goes: presets/watch.json (the watch, unwatch, watches, channel and radar ops), channel.py, which reads the `env` block Claude Code's own .mcp.json format gives an MCP server, radar.py, which imports it, and sources/, the pollers only those ops spawn. The rest of presets/watch/ ships, because gh-prs, gl-mrs, gl-runners and doctor import transport and its siblings from it. With watch gone the claude-channel notifier has no producer, so notifiers/claude-channel/ and the .mcp.json that registers it go too, and release_manifest_drop_keys takes `channels` out of the shipped plugin.json. The validator and formatter READMEs and validators/SCHEMA.md are human documentation nothing reads at run time (checked: no shipped .py opens a README.md or SCHEMA.md).
_kept_why: _shipped_reference.py is NOT denied: it is the fallback _shipped_config() reads when .supertool.json is absent beside _supertool.py (the pip-install route, #1783) -- and this release tree denies .supertool.json, so the fallback is load-bearing here. .mcp.json no longer ships (#2734, _env_word_why).
_keep_why: Exact-path carve-out that wins over a denied prefix (#2729). hooks/shipped_rules.py reads these two files at runtime from $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT for the one shipped jit-context guard rule (supertool-no-cut.md); .claude/ denies the whole directory they live in, so a release install shipped the rule disabled with nothing saying so. shipped_rules.py's own docstring: the rule files are not copied, the same bytes the jit hooks read in this checkout are what a plugin install reads too -- so the fix is to let exactly these two through rather than relocate the source and keep a second copy in sync by hand. Nothing else under .claude/ ships; is_kept() is exact-path only, no prefix.
_budget_why: max_file_bytes and max_files are the directory's own rules (pre-submission checklist, 'Files in the plugin folder'); images and fonts are exempt from the per-file limit. max_total_bytes is this repository's own ceiling: comment/docstring stripping (#2731) took the built tree from 6,887,694 to 3,495,927 bytes (measured on HEAD, 2026-10-03); 4 MiB leaves about 600 KiB of headroom over that for growth before the next release.
_exceptions_why: A declared exception lets check_release_tree.py report a REVIEW line instead of a FAIL for a named, issue-referenced path over max_file_bytes. Any other oversize file still fails -- this is not a second deny-list.
_release_hooks_why: #2734: COMMAND_SCRIPT_NOT_FOLLOWED -- the directory's scanner holds any hook shell script that runs a further file, and hooks.json running the interpreter directly cleared it (probe j, claude-directory-publishing/triggers.md, sixth trigger). Claude Code has no per-platform hook command, so hooks/hooks.release.json carries a literal interpreter ladder in shell form (python3.14 down to python3.9, then py -3, each guarded by a literal identity check; never a bare python3, #572/#1382; no computed command word, the UNPINNED_NPX block) and runs hooks/session_start.py and hooks/pre_bash_guard_hook.py directly. It replaces hooks/hooks.json in the release tree and the three .sh files it no longer needs are dropped. The committed tree keeps the .sh hooks: the source plugin is unchanged until the directory build proves itself. This supersedes #2732's ladder_inline, which inlined python-ladder.sh into the two .sh hooks that now do not ship.
_release_readme_why: #2732: MCP_FORWARDS_CREDENTIAL_ENV's text-only half -- the full README's security section and command examples read as credential-handling/attack text to the directory's scanner. README.release.md is a short, variable-free, URL-free (one real link excepted) description swapped in for README.md at build time; the full README never ships to the directory at all.
_notifiers_deny_why: #2732, from a second validator pass on the full tree. notifiers/claude-channel/README.md and install.sh are human-facing setup docs for a human running them by hand -- the MCP server itself is registered and started by .mcp.json's own command, never by install.sh, and neither file is read at runtime. notifiers/cursor-witness/ is a VS Code extension this repository's own .supertool.json wires in as a dev-only notifier for working on supertool itself; .supertool.json is already denied above and _shipped_reference.py (the fallback a plugin install actually reads) never wires cursor-witness in, so a plugin install never activates it -- the whole directory, icon.png included, ships to no purpose.
